description.narrative: 6 1. Number of public awareness campaigns

comment.narrative: The project launched a comprehensive public awareness campaign to promote Kosovos participation in EU Programmes through a combination of TV spots digital content and community engagement. The campaign included the production of five distinct TV spots one focused on promoting Kosovos overall participation in EU Programmes and four dedicated to specific programmesHorizon Europe Erasmus Plus Creative Europe and the Single Market Programme. These TV spots highlighted the opportunities available within each programme providing clear and accessible information to the public about the benefits and participation requirements.The threemonth media campaign which began in September and will continue until December 2024 is being executed through both TV and digital platforms. The campaign distribution is based on a detailed media plan designed to maximize outreach and engagement ensuring that the messages reach a broad audience. The TV spots are aired across popular channels and digital content is strategically shared through social media and online platforms to further amplify the reach of the campaign.In addition to traditional media the public awareness campaign was complemented by a series of largescale public events such as info days community stands and interactive workshops across key locations in Kosovo. These events were designed to provide facetoface interaction with the public answer questions and guide potential applicants on how to get involved in the EU Programmes. The largescale public campaign also included informational materials and publications distributed to community centers and educational institutions further enhancing the visibility of the EU Programmes.Key ChallengesThe timing of the public awareness campaign was influenced by the status of Kosovos agreements with the EU. Starting the campaign before the agreements were officially signed was seen as potentially creating false expectations among the public. This concern led the project to delay the launch of the campaign until the agreements were finalized. The delay ensured that the campaign was grounded in accurate information and realistic opportunities thereby maintaining the credibility of the project and managing public expectations effectively. Despite this challenge the campaign was successfully launched once the agreements were in place allowing the project to promote Kosovos participation in the EU Programmes confidently and effectively.The campaigns careful planning and broad outreach strategy aimed to increase awareness understanding and engagement with EU Programmes ultimately enhancing Kosovos ability to leverage these opportunities for national development and integration with the EU.

description.narrative: The objective of supporting Kosovos preparation for EU accession and increasing the understanding of EU policies and values has been successfully achieved through enhanced participation in EU Programmes. Key accomplishments include:1.Increased Capacity for EU Programmes: Through targeted capacitybuilding initiatives, stakeholders in Kosovo gained a deeper understanding of EU processes, policies, and values. This was accomplished via specialized training, workshops, and tailored support for programme applicants, significantly improving their ability to engage with EU programmes effectively.2.Expanded Participation in EU Programmes: Kosovos involvement in various EU Programmes has grown, leading to more opportunities for collaboration and integration with EU institutions. This has provided a practical foundation for Kosovos eventual accession by familiarizing local institutions with EU standards and procedures. By the conclusion of the contract Kosovos participation in EU programmes increased dramatically, progressing from zero involvement at the beginning to active participation in 9 distinct EU programmes, including ERASMUS, Horizon Europe, Creative Europe, the Single Market Programme, Citizens, Equality, Rights and Values, Fiscalis, Customs, Digital Europe, and Justice. Additionally, Kosovo was on the verge of signing its 10th agreement under the Employment and Social Innovation (EaSI) strand of the European Social Fund Plus.3.Greater Awareness of EU Values and Policies: The public awareness campaigns and informational sessions helped raise awareness about the EUs fundamental values and principles, contributing to a more informed and supportive public view on Kosovos EU accession process.

description.narrative: The original Terms of Reference (TOR) for Output 3 specified the organization of 12 workshops (2 per each of the 6 EU Programmes), each accommodating 30 participants, for a total of 360 participants. These workshops and seminars were aimed at potential applicants, including representatives from Kosovo institutions and nonpublic sector entities, and were to be held in six major municipalities across Kosovo. Additionally, similar events were planned to guide participants on specific EU Programmes and the preparation of project proposals, resulting in a total of 18 workshops and seminars initially planned under this output.However, the project far exceeded these expectations. Instead of the planned 18 events, the project successfully organized 54 workshops and information sessions, reaching over 660 participants and covering not only the original six EU Programmes but also an additional grantgiving programme, bringing the total to seven. Moreover, the project conducted over 100 tailored workshops and individual consultations, assisting around 300 Kosovo applicants with drafting their project proposals for various EU calls.This significant increase in the number of events, participants, and programmes covered contributed to a broader capacitybuilding effort, ensuring that a wider audience of Kosovo institutions and individuals were better prepared to engage with and apply for EU funding opportunities.

description.narrative: The project has significantly contributed to improving Kosovos absorption of EU Programme funds by strengthening the management and implementation capacities of Kosovos administration and potential beneficiaries. Heres how the objective was achieved:1. Capacity Building for Kosovos Administration: Targeted training and support were provided to government institutions responsible for managing EU Programmes. This included improving their understanding of EU funding mechanisms, compliance requirements, and reporting standards. As a result, the administration is now better equipped to oversee and manage the entire lifecycle of EUfunded projects, from application to implementation.2. Enhanced Coordination Mechanisms: The project facilitated improved coordination between different government bodies and stakeholders involved in EU Programme management. This has streamlined processes, reduced administrative bottlenecks, and ensured more efficient communication between institutions, leading to a higher absorption rate of available funds.Support for Potential Beneficiaries: The project offered specialized assistance to potential beneficiaries, including NGOs, businesses, and civil society organizations. This included providing technical guidance on preparing competitive applications and adhering to EU project implementation standards. This has increased the quality and number of successful applications from Kosovo, leading to better fund absorption.3. Development of Management Tools and Resources: New management tools, templates, and resource materials were developed and made available to Kosovos administration and beneficiaries. These resources have standardized processes and increased the efficiency and transparency of fund management, further improving the absorption rate of EU Programme funds.Through these efforts, the project has significantly reinforced Kosovos ability to manage and utilize EU funds more effectively, positioning the country for greater success in future funding cycles.

Heres how the objective was achieved:1. Capacity Building for Kosovos Administration: Targeted training and support were provided to government institutions responsible for managing EU Programmes. This included improving their understanding of EU funding mechanisms, compliance requirements, and reporting standards. As a result, the administration is now better equipped to oversee and manage the entire lifecycle of EUfunded projects, from application to implementation.2. Enhanced Coordination Mechanisms: The project facilitated improved coordination between different government bodies and stakeholders involved in EU Programme management. This has streamlined processes, reduced administrative bottlenecks, and ensured more efficient communication between institutions, leading to a higher absorption rate of available funds.Support for Potential Beneficiaries: The project offered specialized assistance to potential beneficiaries, including NGOs, businesses, and civil society organizations. This included providing technical guidance on preparing competitive applications and adhering to EU project implementation standards. This has increased the quality and number of successful applications from Kosovo, leading to better fund absorption.3. Development of Management Tools and Resources: New management tools, templates, and resource materials were developed and made available to Kosovos administration and beneficiaries. These resources have standardized processes and increased the efficiency and transparency of fund management, further improving the absorption rate of EU Programme funds.Through these efforts, the project has significantly reinforced Kosovos ability to manage and utilize EU funds more effectively, positioning the country for greater success in future funding cycles.

comment.narrative: The provided text outlines a wellstructured approach to capacity building within the context of facilitating EU programmes at the national level. It highlights the importance of the Training Needs Analysis TNA in identifying gaps in knowledge and expertise among key stakeholders including the NIPACDevelopment Cooperation Office National Contact Points NCPs and line ministries. The TNA served as the foundation for targeted interventions such as training sessions and handson support ensuring that the staff involved were equipped to manage EU programmes effectively.The continuous nature of the TNA is also crucial. As new staff members replaced outgoing NIPAC and NCP personnel the ongoing assessment ensured that the training was up to date and relevant to the evolving team. This adaptive approach likely contributed to the projects sustainability by building a knowledgeable workforce capable of facilitating EU programmes over the long term.Overall this methodology demonstrates a thoughtful and responsive strategy for improving institutional capacity and promoting the successful implementation of EU programmes in a dynamic organizational environment. It shows a clear understanding of the need for both initial training and ongoing support which is essential when working with complex evolving structures.

By the conclusion of the threeyear project the NIPAC OfficeDevelopment Cooperation Office had made substantial progress in enhancing its ability to coordinate and oversee the National Contact Points NCPs for the 9 EU programmes in which Kosovo is actively involved. This improvement in capacity was a key outcome of the project as the NIPAC Office became more adept at managing the diverse responsibilities associated with these programmes.Throughout the project several NCPs were replaced yet despite these transitions the project team is confident that the current NCPs possess the necessary knowledge and organizational structures to successfully manage and facilitate the EU programmes at the national level. They are now equipped to conduct informative events such as info days to engage and guide potential applicants through the application process. Furthermore the NCPs have achieved full control over the operational aspects of the EU programmes in which Kosovo participates ensuring smooth coordination and communication.In addition to these responsibilities the NCPs have gained proficiency in utilizing the various online tools that support the submission and management of applications for different calls for proposals. This technical expertise enables them to effectively monitor and assist potential applicants providing guidance from the initial stages of application to the final stages of participation in EUfunded initiatives. The comprehensive development of these capacities ensures that the NCPs are wellpositioned to continue facilitating Kosovos involvement in EU programmes fostering greater integration and collaboration at the European level.

description.narrative: To achieve Output 1, which focuses on delivering a Training Needs Assessment Report and a comprehensive training plan for National Contact Points (NCPs), relevant institutions, and potential applicants (including awarded grantees), the following steps were undertaken:1. Training Needs Assessment: A detailed assessment was conducted to identify the specific skills and knowledge gaps among NCPs, government institutions, and potential applicants (including grantees). This assessment involved surveys, interviews, and consultations with key stakeholders to understand their existing capacities and the challenges they face in applying for and managing EU Programmes. The assessment report outlined the key areas for development, such as knowledge of EU regulations, proposal writing, project management, financial reporting, and compliance with EU standards.2. Development of a Tailored Training Plan: Based on the findings of the training needs assessment, a targeted training plan was designed to address the specific gaps identified. The training plan was customized to meet the unique requirements of NCPs, relevant institutions, and potential applicants, ensuring that each group received the most relevant and practical training.3. Organizing Training Sessions: A series of tailored workshops and training sessions were organized to equip participants with the necessary skills to engage with EU Programmes. These workshops focused on practical aspects, such as how to prepare competitive applications, how to comply with EU funding requirements, and effective project management techniques.4. Information Days: A large number of information days were held to raise awareness about available EU Programmes and to provide guidance on the application process. These events were open to all potential applicants and relevant stakeholders, serving as a platform for direct interaction with experts, the project team, and NCPs.These info days also served to clarify programme objectives, eligibility criteria, and the steps needed to access EU funding.5. Support for National Contact Points (NCPs): Dedicated workshops and mentoring sessions were organized specifically for the National Contact Points. These sessions helped NCPs to better understand their roles in guiding and supporting potential applicants, ensuring that they were wellequipped to provide technical assistance and facilitate communication between the applicants and the EU.6. Customized Support for Potential Applicants and Grantees: Potential applicants and awarded grantees received customized workshops that focused on the application process, project implementation, and reporting requirements. This ensured that participants were better prepared to handle the administrative and financial aspects of EUfunded projects, reducing the risk of noncompliance.7. Ongoing Mentorship and Followup: Following the workshops and training sessions, participants were provided with ongoing mentorship and support to apply the knowledge they had gained. This included oneonone coaching, technical advice, and followup sessions to address any emerging issues or questions.By implementing these targeted training initiatives, the project effectively enhanced the capacities of NCPs, relevant institutions, and potential applicants, ensuring they were wellprepared to successfully engage with EU Programmes. The Training Needs Assessment Report and Training Plan were critical tools in tailoring these interventions to meet the specific needs of all stakeholders involved.

description.narrative: Provision of trainings to staff of individual entities on Project Cycle Management

comment.narrative: The above description provides a clear and wellorganized assessment of a key challenge faced at the beginning of the project namely the lack of capacity in Project Cycle Management PCM. It effectively draws attention to the findings of the Training Needs Assessment Report and Training Plan emphasizing the importance of these tools in diagnosing the skills gap within Kosovos efforts to participate in EU programmes. By pointing out that only a few National Contact Points NCPs had been appointed in select ministries the description highlights the initial steps taken but stresses their insufficiency in addressing the broader needs of the project.One of the strengths of the description is its recognition that the lack of PCM training extended beyond government structures to include public and private entities such as civil society organizations. This inclusion of a wide range of stakeholders underscores the breadth of the problem and shows how deeply it affected Kosovos ability to successfully engage with EU programmes. The emphasis on civil society and private sector actors is particularly important as these groups play a vital role in applying for and managing EUfunded projects.The description also clearly identifies the complexity of the project lifecyclefrom proposal development to implementation and monitoringand how the lack of specialized knowledge in these areas hindered Kosovos readiness to fully participate in EU programmes. This not only provides insight into the specific nature of the skills gap but also adds weight to the argument for the urgency of targeted capacitybuilding efforts.

By the conclusion of the Intervention a diverse range of stakeholders and beneficiary groups had completed extensive and comprehensive training on Project Cycle Management PCM. These training sessions were specifically designed to equip Kosovo applicants for EU Programmes with the skills and knowledge needed to successfully navigate every phase of the project lifecycle from the initial planning and proposal development through to the implementation execution monitoring evaluation and reporting stages. The trainings addressed essential elements of PCM including project design risk management budgeting and the application of relevant tools and methodologies to ensure projects were executed efficiently and achieved their objectives.The training programme targeted a broad array of stakeholderssuch as National Contact Points NCPs government ministries civil society organizations public institutions private entities and other relevant bodies. This comprehensive approach effectively built the capacity of these groups to write project proposals manage and coordinate EUfunded projects and initiatives at the international national and local levels. Beyond enhancing their technical competencies the trainings also fostered improved collaboration and communication among the various actors involved contributing to more successful and sustainable project outcomes.Throughout the projects duration over 100 individual training sessions and around 54 workshops were delivered to the target groups reaching approximately 600 potential applicants. This extensive effort helped strengthen Kosovos ability to engage effectively with EU programmes and ensure longterm project success.

The assessment report outlined the key areas for development, such as knowledge of EU regulations, proposal writing, project management, financial reporting, and compliance with EU standards.2. Development of a Tailored Training Plan: Based on the findings of the training needs assessment, a targeted training plan was designed to address the specific gaps identified. The training plan was customized to meet the unique requirements of NCPs, relevant institutions, and potential applicants, ensuring that each group received the most relevant and practical training.3. Organizing Training Sessions: A series of tailored workshops and training sessions were organized to equip participants with the necessary skills to engage with EU Programmes. These workshops focused on practical aspects, such as how to prepare competitive applications, how to comply with EU funding requirements, and effective project management techniques.4. Information Days: A large number of information days were held to raise awareness about available EU Programmes and to provide guidance on the application process. These events were open to all potential applicants and relevant stakeholders, serving as a platform for direct interaction with experts, the project team, and NCPs.These info days also served to clarify programme objectives, eligibility criteria, and the steps needed to access EU funding.5. Support for National Contact Points (NCPs): Dedicated workshops and mentoring sessions were organized specifically for the National Contact Points. These sessions helped NCPs to better understand their roles in guiding and supporting potential applicants, ensuring that they were wellequipped to provide technical assistance and facilitate communication between the applicants and the EU.6. Customized Support for Potential Applicants and Grantees: Potential applicants and awarded grantees received customized workshops that focused on the application process, project implementation, and reporting requirements. This ensured that participants were better prepared to handle the administrative and financial aspects of EUfunded projects, reducing the risk of noncompliance.7. Ongoing Mentorship and Followup: Following the workshops and training sessions, participants were provided with ongoing mentorship and support to apply the knowledge they had gained. This included oneonone coaching, technical advice, and followup sessions to address any emerging issues or questions.By implementing these targeted training initiatives, the project effectively enhanced the capacities of NCPs, relevant institutions, and potential applicants, ensuring they were wellprepared to successfully engage with EU Programmes. The Training Needs Assessment Report and Training Plan were critical tools in tailoring these interventions to meet the specific needs of all stakeholders involved.

comment.narrative: The project team has supported by NCPs to finalise their applications for the annual operational grant.

4 eligible programmes have successfully received annual operational grants which include Creative Europe Erasmus Fiscalis and Customs. These grants provide essential financial support for the ongoing management and facilitation of these EU programmes allowing for smoother implementation and greater impact at the national level. It is also anticipated that the Citizens Equality Rights and Values CERV programme will secure an annual operational grant further contributing to its capacity to support various initiatives. However at this stage the National Contact Point NCP responsible for the CERV programme has not yet made a final decision on whether to proceed with the application for this grant. The decisionmaking process is ongoing and the outcome will determine whether the programme can benefit from the same level of financial support as the other eligible programmes. This uncertainty highlights the need for careful consideration and strategic planning by the NCP to ensure that Kosovo maximizes its opportunities for support and engagement in EUfunded programmes.From 9 EU Programmes in which Kosovo participates at the end of the project only the 4 EU Programmes mentioned are eligible to receive an national operational grant.
